facts.heading: GP suggested visit due to exhaustion
facts.content: Daniel's GP suggested he come to therapy because she observed that he looks exhausted.
facts.evidence: My GP suggested I come. She said I look exhausted, and she's right, I am.

facts.heading: Burnout started in October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burned out since October.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burned out since October.

facts.heading: Workload increased after client loss
facts.content: Daniel's company lost a big client, and he ended up doing three people's jobs.
facts.evidence: We lost a big client, and half the team got moved onto the rescue plan, so I ended up doing three people's jobs.

facts.heading: Works long hours daily
facts.content: Daniel starts work at seven and continues answering messages until ten at night.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by seven and I'm still answering messages at ten at night.

facts.heading: Sleep is terrible, four hours
facts.content: Daniel sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours.

facts.heading: Wakes at three AM
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: I wake up at three in the morning and can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Dreading the nights
facts.content: Daniel has started dreading the nights.
facts.evidence: I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: My father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's age and condition
facts.content: Daniel's father is seventy-three years old and experiences shaking hands and slowness.
facts.evidence: He's seventy-three and he's always been the strong one.

facts.heading: Drives father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds for neurology appointments every few weeks.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds. The neurology appointments are every few weeks, and it's an hour each way.

facts.heading: Hannah lives in Toronto
facts.content: Daniel's younger sister, Hannah, lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: My younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto, so all the care for our father falls on me.

facts.heading: Feels guilty about being tired
facts.content: Daniel feels it is selfish to be tired while his father is ill.
facts.evidence: I feel it's selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill.

facts.heading: Tells sister he is fine
facts.content: When his sister asks how he is, Daniel tells her he is fine.
facts.evidence: She asks how I am and I say fine.

facts.heading: Cannot face hospital visits
facts.content: Daniel sometimes sits in the hospital car park for ten minutes before going in.
facts.evidence: That some days I sit in the car park at the hospital for ten minutes before I go in, because I can't face it.

facts.heading: GP found stress and exhaustion
facts.content: Daniel's GP ran blood tests which were all normal. The GP attributed his symptoms to stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She said it's stress and exhaustion

facts.heading: Girlfriend booked therapy appointment
facts.content: Claire booked the therapy appointment for Daniel.
facts.evidence: My girlfriend booked it, to be honest. Claire

facts.heading: Claire is patient but strained
facts.content: Claire is patient and makes Daniel tea, but Daniel sees that it is wearing on her.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Stopped accepting weekend trips
facts.content: Claire stopped asking Daniel if he wanted to go away for the weekend.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend

facts.heading: Fear of emails prevents travel
facts.content: Daniel fears that if he travels, he will return to two hundred emails.
facts.evidence: If I'm away I'll come back to two hundred of them

facts.heading: Dad might need assistance
facts.content: Daniel is concerned that his Dad might need something.
facts.evidence: And Dad might need something

facts.heading: Stopped running two months ago
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago

facts.heading: Ran ten kilometres for six years
facts.content: Daniel used to run ten kilometres every Saturday morning for six years.
facts.evidence: I ran. Ten kilometres every Saturday morning. I'd done it for six years.

facts.heading: Work emails sent late
facts.content: Daniel's boss, Peterson, sends emails at eleven at night.
facts.evidence: he sends emails at eleven at night

facts.heading: Boss expects early replies
facts.content: Daniel's boss expects an answer to emails before breakfast.
facts.evidence: and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Answers boss's emails always
facts.content: Daniel answers his boss's emails every time, even when in bed.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss due to commitment
facts.content: Daniel fears his boss will think he isn't committed if he doesn't answer emails.
facts.evidence: That he'd think I wasn't committed.

facts.heading: Restructuring planned for spring
facts.content: There is a restructuring planned for the spring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring in the spring

facts.heading: Mortgage is a financial factor
facts.content: Daniel has a mortgage.
facts.evidence: I have a mortgage.

facts.heading: Mood is mostly flat and irritable
facts.content: Daniel's mood is mostly flat and irritable.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable.

facts.heading: Snapped at colleague last week
facts.content: Daniel snapped at a colleague last week over nothing.
facts.evidence: I snapped at a colleague last week over nothing

facts.heading: Experienced physical symptoms in toilet
facts.content: Daniel experienced his heart racing and hands shaking in the toilet.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking.

facts.heading: Past episodes of panic
facts.content: Daniel has experienced episodes like this a couple of times. One occurred on the train to Manchester.
facts.evidence: A couple of times. Once on the train to Manchester.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel fears that he is losing it or that he is not coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up like, I don't know. Not coping.

facts.heading: Coping with anxiety via substances
facts.content: Daniel drinks about two to three glasses of wine in the evenings to switch his head off. He also drinks about six cups of coffee a day.
facts.evidence: I'm on about six cups a day. And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Feeling uneasy about wine
facts.content: Daniel feels uneasy about the wine, and notes it only works for an hour before he wakes up at three.
facts.evidence: Uneasy. It works for an hour and then I wake at three anyway.

facts.heading: Relief from sharing burdens
facts.content: Daniel felt a sense of relief after sharing his burdens, comparing it to putting down a bag.
facts.evidence: A bit of a relief, actually. Like putting down a bag I didn't realise I was carrying.

facts.heading: Sleep as primary need
facts.content: Daniel believes that if he could sleep, he could cope with the rest of his issues.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Family's stoic nature
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather and father both worked in the mines in Yorkshire and never complained about anything.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything, not once.

facts.heading: Daniel's self-perception
facts.content: Daniel feels he is the same as his father and grandfather, and worries his father would think he was weak for being there.
facts.evidence: I'm the same. I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.heading: Daniel's feeling of being tired
facts.content: Daniel stated that he is not weak, but just very tired.
facts.evidence: That I'm not weak. I'm just very tired.

facts.heading: Plan for evening routine
facts.content: Daniel agreed to try turning off his phone at half past nine in the evening, possibly with Claire while having tea on the sofa.
facts.evidence: Yes. Half past nine, perhaps. I could make it a thing with Claire. Tea on the sofa.

facts.heading: Plan to track sleep
facts.content: Daniel agreed to write down when he wakes up, if he wakes up.
facts.evidence: I'll write down when I wake up, if I wake up.

facts.heading: Next appointment scheduled
facts.content: Daniel will attend the next session next week.
facts.evidence: Yes. I'll be here.

facts.heading: Trains are difficult for Daniel
facts.content: Daniel finds the trains to be awful.
facts.evidence: the trains are awful
